content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

The employee is Jesus Cooke (E029), requesting write access to Source Code.

There are two conflicting notes:
- Note 1 says: full_time Payroll Specialist, recommend write.
- Note 2 says: contractor with basic security training, recommend read.

The two notes conflict on employment type. Note 2 says Note 1 was incorrect ("not full-time as previously noted"). The security DB shows contractor.

Access policy:
- full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if role owns system. Payroll Specialist doesn't own Source Code (Engineer owns it), so max write.
- contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin. This contractor has basic training, so max read.

Given conflicting information, which to trust? Note 2 explicitly corrects Note 1 as a correction from the Security DB. The notes are from HR agent and Security agent. The Security DB note seems more authoritative about employment type. Typically in these scenarios, the second note is the correction and the final facts should be the contractor with basic security training.

So the employee is a contractor with basic security training → max access is read. Requested write > maximum, so grant maximum = read.

Let me submit decision: read.

Evidence: Employee is a contractor with basic security training per Security DB; contractors without advanced training max out at read; requested write exceeds max, so grant read.

The two notes conflict on employment type. Note 2 comes from the Security DB and explicitly corrects Note 1, stating Jesus Cooke is a contractor with basic security training (not full-time). Under policy, contractors without advanced security training max out at read. The requested write exceeds that maximum, so I grant the maximum allowed level.
